conditions: Sequential benchmark processes; no simultaneous benchmark loads
Synthetic messages and in-memory HTTP responses; no QQ or database connection
CPU affinity and filesystem cache state not controlled

method.throughput: Two independent processes, five rounds each, original repository harness unchanged; pooled ten-round median including every sample.
method.latency: Separate diagnostic process, five rounds; nearest-rank quantiles recomputed from all per-event traces for each case; warmup excluded.
method.memory: Fresh process per case, one round; sampled RSS during measured work, then GC snapshots with retained cache, after close and after 100 ms idle.
method.gc: Explicit GC between cases; extra diagnostic GC and file I/O occur outside event timing.
method.workload: Serial synthetic C2C events with in-memory native Response fixtures; SDK default queue/cache settings. No QQ network or database.
method.timingScope: Includes event construction, JSON byte length calculation, SDK dispatch, mock HTTP, and awaiting completion; excludes real network

historicalComparability.conclusion: Historical results use earlier runtime source and a different observation time. No speedup/regression attribution or statistical significance claim is made.

rawThroughputRuns.workload: Serial synthetic QQ events; native Response bodies without real networking; 64 KiB synthetic image bytes; a 513-value enumeration; default capacities. The pressure case measures correct overload rejection after filling 10000 retained reply scopes. RSS is sampled, not a peak or leak measurement. Compare identical harnesses on the same host.

rawDiagnosticRun.percentileDefinition: Nearest rank on measured serial dispatch durations; warmup excluded
rawDiagnosticRun.timingScope: Includes event construction, JSON byte length calculation, SDK dispatch, mock HTTP, and awaiting completion; excludes real network
rawDiagnosticRun.instrumentation: Two performance.now calls and a Float64Array write per event. Sorting, extra GC, snapshots and raw-file output are outside the measured loop. Throughput from this diagnostic is not the uninstrumented benchmark.
rawDiagnosticRun.memoryLimitations: Process snapshots include Node, fixtures, live diagnostic arrays and retained SDK state. Post-close GC is a point observation, not a multi-day leak test. Public queue/cache/prompt counters are asserted, not untracked private resources.

limits: Single-process serial microbenchmark; CPU affinity and background load were not controlled.
No real QQ traffic, platform quotas, database, concurrent business workload, 2000-group traffic or long-duration soak was exercised.
Latency probes include timer/array instrumentation and therefore are separate from the unchanged throughput runs.
RSS is process memory including Node and fixtures; samples do not establish the true peak or SDK-only allocation.
Memory snapshots after close do not prove long-term absence of leaks.
The pressure scenario measures rejection speed, not accepted business throughput.
Events enter execution.accept directly; WS/Webhook transport, incoming body JSON parsing and signature verification are outside this measurement.
